notes.front: Should hydrometer readings be taken before or after adding distilled water?
notes.back: Always before, never after.
notes.explanation: Added water needs time to mix, or the sample drawn will not represent the true strength.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Lead-Acid Battery Testing Methods”, PDF p. 532
notes.evidence: Always take hydrometer readings before adding distilled water, never after.

notes.front: A lead-acid aircraft battery at 80 °F reads 1.220 on the hydrometer. How is it rated, and what is needed?
notes.back: D) Low state of charge; it needs immediate recharging
notes.choices:
A) High state of charge; no action
B) Medium state of charge; recheck next inspection
C) Fully discharged; replace it
D) Low state of charge; it needs immediate recharging
notes.choicesExplained: A) High charge is 1.275 to 1.300. B) Medium is 1.240 to 1.275. C) 1.220 is within the low band, which calls for recharging, not replacement.
notes.explanation: 1.220 falls in the low band (1.240 to 1.200), and a battery that low is considered in need of immediate recharging; 80 °F needs no correction.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Lead-Acid Battery Testing Methods”, PDF p. 531
notes.evidence: An aircraft battery in a low state of charge may have perhaps 50 percent charge remaining, but is nevertheless considered low in the face of heavy demands that would soon exhaust it.

notes.front: Why must the charging voltage of a lead-acid battery exceed its open-circuit voltage?
notes.back: To overcome the voltage drop caused by the battery’s internal resistance.
notes.explanation: A fully charged 12-cell battery reads about 26.4 volts open-circuit but needs about 28 volts to charge.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Lead-Acid Battery Charging Methods”, PDF p. 532
notes.evidence: Because of the internal resistance (IR) in the battery, the voltage of the external charging source must be greater than the open circuit voltage.

notes.front: What is the drawback of constant current charging compared with constant voltage charging?
notes.back: It takes longer and, near the end, risks overcharging if care is not taken.
notes.explanation: In constant current charging, the current stays almost the same throughout.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Lead-Acid Battery Charging Methods”, PDF p. 532
notes.evidence: This method requires a longer time to charge a battery fully and, toward the end of the process, presents the danger of overcharging, if care is not exercised.

notes.front: The aircraft’s own generator system recharges the battery in flight. Which charging method is this?
notes.back: Constant voltage.
notes.explanation: The generator’s voltage is held constant by its voltage regulator.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Lead-Acid Battery Charging Methods”, PDF p. 532
notes.evidence: This method of charging is the constant voltage method, since the generator voltage is held constant by use of a voltage regulator.

notes.front: What precautions does the Handbook give against igniting the gases from a battery on charge?
notes.back: Loosen the vent caps but leave them in place, and allow no flames, sparks or other ignition sources nearby.
notes.explanation: A charging battery gives off hydrogen and oxygen, an explosive mixture.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Lead-Acid Battery Charging Methods”, PDF p. 532
notes.evidence: Loosen the vent caps and leave in place. Do not permit open flames, sparks, or other sources of ignition in the vicinity.

notes.front: If lead-acid battery electrolyte gets on the skin, what should be done?
notes.back: Wash the area thoroughly with water, then apply bicarbonate of soda.
notes.explanation: Sulfuric acid burns clothing and skin.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Lead-Acid Battery Charging Methods”, PDF p. 532
notes.evidence: If the acid does contact the skin, wash the area thoroughly with water and then apply bicarbonate of soda.

notes.front: How is nickel-cadmium electrolyte spilled on hands or clothes neutralised?
notes.back: Immediately with vinegar or dilute boric acid solution, then rinsed with clear water.
notes.explanation: The potassium hydroxide electrolyte is caustic, so goggles, plastic gloves and an apron are worn.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “General Maintenance and Safety Precautions”, PDF p. 533
notes.evidence: In case of spillage on hands or clothes, neutralize the alkali immediately with vinegar or dilute boric acid solution (one pound per gallon of water); then rinse with clear water.

notes.front: While a lead-acid battery is being tested, electrolyte splashes on a technician’s forearm. What is the right first aid?
notes.back: D) Wash thoroughly with water, then apply bicarbonate of soda
notes.choices:
A) Neutralise it with vinegar, then rinse
B) Leave it to dry and report it later
C) Wipe it off and apply boric acid solution
D) Wash thoroughly with water, then apply bicarbonate of soda
notes.choicesExplained: A) Vinegar is for the alkaline electrolyte of nickel-cadmium batteries. C) Boric acid is also for nickel-cadmium spills. B) Sulfuric acid burns skin, so it must be dealt with at once.
notes.explanation: Lead-acid electrolyte is sulfuric acid: wash with water, then neutralise with bicarbonate of soda.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Lead-Acid Battery Charging Methods”, PDF p. 532
notes.evidence: Handle the electrolyte carefully because sulfuric acid burns clothing and skin. If the acid does contact the skin, wash the area thoroughly with water and then apply bicarbonate of soda.

notes.front: A partly discharged NiCad battery shows a low electrolyte level. What should the technician do?
notes.back: A) Charge it fully, then add water if needed
notes.choices:
A) Charge it fully, then add water if needed
B) Top it up with electrolyte now
C) Top it up with water now
D) Replace the battery
notes.choicesExplained: C) The level rises on recharge, so topping up now adds too much. B) The level is low because the plates have absorbed electrolyte, not because it is lost. D) A low level while discharged is normal.
notes.explanation: The level rises on recharge and is highest at full charge, so water is added only then.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Operation of Nickel-Cadmium Cells”, PDF p. 533
notes.evidence: Therefore, water should be added only when the battery is fully charged.

notes.front: Before a NiCad battery replaces a lead-acid one, what must be done to the battery compartment?
notes.back: Clean, dry and free it of all acid; wash and neutralise it with ammonia or boric acid, dry it, and paint it with alkali-resisting varnish.
notes.explanation: Traces of the old battery’s acid must not remain where the alkaline battery will sit.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Operation of Nickel-Cadmium Cells”, PDF p. 533
notes.evidence: The compartment must be washed out and neutralized with ammonia or boric acid solution, allowed to dry thoroughly, and then painted with an alkali resisting varnish.

notes.front: An aircraft’s lead-acid battery is being replaced with a NiCad. The compartment shows traces of old acid. What must happen before installation?
notes.back: C) Wash and neutralise it, let it dry, and paint it with alkali-resisting varnish
notes.choices:
A) Nothing; the batteries are interchangeable as they are
B) Wipe it dry and fit the new battery
C) Wash and neutralise it, let it dry, and paint it with alkali-resisting varnish
D) Refill the sump pad with sodium bicarbonate
notes.choicesExplained: A) They are usually interchangeable electrically, but the compartment must first be cleared of acid. B) Drying alone leaves the acid traces. D) For a NiCad the pad takes a boric acid solution.
notes.explanation: The compartment must be free of all acid, neutralised, dried and varnished against alkali.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Operation of Nickel-Cadmium Cells”, PDF p. 533
notes.evidence: When replacing a lead-acid battery with a nickel-cadmium battery, the battery compartment must be clean, dry, and free of all traces of acid from the old battery.

notes.front: Which hazard sets aircraft lithium-ion batteries apart from other rechargeable types?
notes.back: C) A flammable, pressurised electrolyte that can overheat and burn
notes.choices:
A) Spilled sulfuric acid
B) A caustic potassium hydroxide electrolyte
C) A flammable, pressurised electrolyte that can overheat and burn
D) Voltage depression after standby use
notes.choicesExplained: A) Sulfuric acid is the lead-acid electrolyte. B) Potassium hydroxide is the nickel-cadmium electrolyte. D) Voltage depression is a nickel-cadmium trait.
notes.explanation: Unlike other rechargeables, lithium-ion cells contain a flammable electrolyte and are kept pressurised.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Lithium-Ion Batteries”, PDF p. 534
notes.evidence: Under certain conditions, they can overheat and a fire can occur.

notes.front: What advantages do static inverters have over rotary inverters in aircraft?
notes.back: No moving parts and suitability for conduction cooling; they are also smaller and lighter.
notes.explanation: They use solid-state components and can now meet any requirement rotary inverters fill.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Static Inverters”, PDF p. 536
notes.evidence: This type of equipment has certain advantages for aircraft applications, particularly the absence of moving parts and the adaptability to conduction cooling.

notes.front: An inverter is essentially a direct current motor driving an alternating current generator in one housing. Rotary or static?
notes.back: Rotary.
notes.explanation: Static inverters use solid-state components and have no moving parts.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Rotary Inverters”, PDF p. 535
notes.evidence: Such inverters are essentially AC generators and DC motors in one housing.

notes.front: What is doping?
notes.back: Adding small amounts of impurities to a semiconductor to increase its current flow by adding a few electrons or holes.
notes.explanation: Doped material falls into one of two types: N-type or P-type.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Doping”, PDF p. 537
notes.evidence: Doping is the process by which small amounts of additives called impurities are added to the semiconductor material to increase their current flow by adding a few electrons or a few holes.

notes.front: A semiconductor is doped with an acceptor impurity. Is it N-type or P-type?
notes.back: P-type.
notes.explanation: Donor impurities make N-type material; acceptor impurities make P-type.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Doping”, PDF p. 537
notes.evidence: A P-type semiconductor is one that is doped with a P-type or an acceptor impurity.

notes.front: What happens when a diode is reverse biased?
notes.back: Current does not flow, and the depletion zone widens.
notes.explanation: The applied voltage acts in the same direction as the depletion zone’s own field, pulling carriers away from the junction.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Reverse Biased Diode”, PDF p. 540
notes.evidence: When the battery is turned around as shown in Figure 12-213, then the diode is reverse biased and current does not flow. The most noticeable effect seen is the widened depletion zone.

notes.front: A diode’s P-type side is connected to the positive terminal of a supply and its N-type side to the negative. What happens?
notes.back: B) It conducts with very little resistance
notes.choices:
A) It blocks current and its depletion zone widens
B) It conducts with very little resistance
C) It breaks down and is destroyed
D) It gives out light whatever its type
notes.choicesExplained: A) That is reverse bias, with the supply the other way round. C) Forward bias is normal operation, not breakdown. D) Only a light-emitting diode is designed to give out light.
notes.explanation: Positive to P and negative to N is forward bias, and a forward-biased diode offers very little resistance.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Forward Biased Diode”, PDF p. 540
notes.evidence: To summarize, the important thing to remember is that these PN junction diodes offer very little resistance to current when the diode is forward biased.

notes.front: How does the output of a full-wave rectifier differ from a half-wave rectifier’s?
notes.back: It is a continuous sequence of pulses, without the gaps the half-wave output has.
notes.explanation: A half-wave rectifier passes only one half of each cycle, leaving gaps between pulses.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Full-Wave Rectifier”, PDF p. 543
notes.evidence: The term “full-wave” indicates that the output is a continuous sequence of pulses rather than having gaps that appear in the half-wave rectifier.

notes.front: An alternator’s output must feed a direct current bus. Which device converts it?
notes.back: D) A rectifier
notes.choices:
A) An inverter
B) A transformer
C) A current transformer
D) A rectifier
notes.choicesExplained: A) An inverter does the reverse, direct to alternating. B) A transformer changes alternating voltage, not its form. C) A current transformer senses line current for protection.
notes.explanation: A rectifier turns alternating current into direct current by limiting the direction of flow.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Rectifiers”, PDF p. 541
notes.evidence: A rectifier is a device that transforms AC into DC by limiting or regulating the direction of current flow.

notes.front: A circuit needs a simple part to hold a steady voltage across a load despite small supply changes. Which component fits?
notes.back: C) A Zener diode
notes.choices:
A) A thermistor
B) A light-emitting diode
C) A Zener diode
D) A rheostat
notes.choicesExplained: A) A thermistor’s resistance follows temperature. B) A light-emitting diode gives light; it is not a regulator. D) A rheostat must be adjusted by hand to change current.
notes.explanation: Within its range, a Zener diode acts as a voltage regulator.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Zener Diodes”, PDF p. 544
notes.evidence: Within the normal operating range, the zener functions as a voltage regulator, waveform clipper, and other related functions.

notes.front: On a transistor symbol, what does the emitter arrow show?
notes.back: Its type: pointing in is PNP, pointing out is NPN.
notes.explanation: The angled line carrying the arrow is the emitter; the one without is the collector.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Identification of Transistors”, PDF p. 547
notes.evidence: The direction of the arrow on the emitter determines whether or not the transistor is a PNP or an NPN type.

notes.front: A transistor has a thin region of P-material between two regions of N-type material. Which class is it?
notes.back: NPN.
notes.explanation: Transistors are classed by the arrangement of their N and P materials.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Classification”, PDF p. 546
notes.evidence: The NPN transistor is formed by introducing a thin region of P-material between two regions of N-type material.

notes.front: What are the three common transistor configurations?
notes.back: Common-emitter, common-collector and common-base.
notes.explanation: The Handbook shows each one in both NPN and PNP form.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Common Transistor Configurations”, PDF p. 552
notes.evidence: NPN PNP Output Input Output Input Common-emitter NPN PNP Output Input Output Input Common-collector NPN Input PNP Output Input Output Common-base

notes.front: What does a low-pass filter do?
notes.back: It passes low frequencies well and attenuates frequencies above its cut-off.
notes.explanation: A high-pass filter does the opposite.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Low-Pass Filter”, PDF p. 553
notes.evidence: A low-pass filter is a filter that passes low frequencies well, but attenuates (reduces) higher frequencies.

notes.front: In a Class A amplifier, for how much of the input signal does the transistor conduct, and what is the trade-off?
notes.back: All of it (360°); it is the least efficient class but has the best fidelity.
notes.explanation: Class B conducts for 50 percent and is twice as efficient; Class C conducts for less than 50 percent.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Class A”, PDF p. 555
notes.evidence: In the Class A operation, the current in the transistor flows for 100 percent or 360° of the input signal. [Figure 12-238] Class A operation is the least efficient class of operation but provides the best fidelity.

notes.front: What are the two broad classes of logic polarity?
notes.back: Positive polarity and negative polarity.
notes.explanation: The manufacturer’s logic diagrams usually state the voltage levels and which polarity is used.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Logic Polarity”, PDF p. 561
notes.evidence: Logic circuits are usually divided into two broad classes: positive polarity and negative polarity.

notes.front: What does an inverter logic gate do?
notes.back: It inverts its input: a high input gives a low output, and a low input a high output.
notes.explanation: In binary terms, it turns a 1 into a 0 or a 0 into a 1.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “The Inverter Logic”, PDF p. 562
notes.evidence: When a high voltage is applied to the inverter input, low voltage is the output. When a low voltage is applied to the input, a high voltage is on the output.

notes.front: When is the output of an AND gate high?
notes.back: Only when all of its inputs are high.
notes.explanation: If any input is low, the output is low.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “The AND Gate”, PDF p. 562
notes.evidence: The operation of the AND gate is such that the output is high only when all of the inputs are high.

notes.front: When is the output of an OR gate low?
notes.back: Only when there are no high levels on any input.
notes.explanation: Any high input makes the OR gate’s output high.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “The OR Gate”, PDF p. 563
notes.evidence: The only time that a low is produced on the output is if there are no high levels on any input.

notes.front: When is the output of a NAND gate low?
notes.back: Only if all of its inputs are high.
notes.explanation: A NAND gate is an AND function with an inverted output.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “The NAND Gate”, PDF p. 563
notes.evidence: The logical operation of the NAND gate is such that a low output occurs only if all inputs are high.

notes.front: What makes the output of a NOR gate low?
notes.back: Any of its inputs being high.
notes.explanation: A NOR gate is an OR function with an inverted output.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “The NOR Gate”, PDF p. 563
notes.evidence: The logical operation of the NOR gate is such that a low output happens when any of its inputs are high.

notes.front: A two-input gate gives a low output only when both inputs are high; any low input gives a high output. Which gate is it?
notes.back: B) NAND
notes.choices:
A) AND
B) NAND
C) OR
D) NOR
notes.choicesExplained: A) An AND gate’s output is high when all inputs are high. C) An OR gate’s output is low only when no input is high. D) A NOR gate’s output is low when any input is high.
notes.explanation: That is the AND function inverted, which is the NAND gate.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “The NAND Gate”, PDF p. 563
notes.evidence: The logical operation of the NAND gate is such that a low output occurs only if all inputs are high. If any of the inputs are low, the output is high.

notes.front: Why would a designer choose an integrated circuit over the same logic built from discrete components?
notes.back: A) It is smaller, uses less power and is very reliable
notes.choices:
A) It is smaller, uses less power and is very reliable
B) It is larger and easier to repair by hand
C) It needs no protection from static electricity
D) It must be larger than discrete parts to save power
notes.choicesExplained: B) The integrated circuit is much smaller, not larger. C) Integrated circuits are among the parts most often damaged by electrostatic discharge. D) An integrated circuit is both smaller and lower in power use than discrete parts.
notes.explanation: The Handbook lists small size, lower power use, reliability and low cost as its advantages.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “The Integrated Circuit”, PDF p. 563
notes.evidence: In most cases, the IC has an advantage over the use of discrete components in that they are smaller, consume less power, are very reliable, and are inexpensive.

notes.front: In the Airman Certification Standards’ digital logic element, what does RAM stand for?
notes.back: Random Access Memory.
notes.explanation: The standards name it with ROM and NVRAM under digital logic.
notes.source: Aviation Mechanic General, Airframe, and Powerplant ACS Companion Guide, “Appendix: Abbreviations and Acronyms”, PDF p. 27
notes.evidence: RAM Random Access Memory

notes.front: In the Airman Certification Standards’ digital logic element, what does ROM stand for?
notes.back: Read-Only Memory.
notes.explanation: It is one of three memory types named in the standards’ digital logic element.
notes.source: Aviation Mechanic General, Airframe, and Powerplant ACS Companion Guide, “Appendix: Abbreviations and Acronyms”, PDF p. 27
notes.evidence: RAM Random Access Memory ROM Read-Only Memory

notes.front: In the Airman Certification Standards’ digital logic element, what does NVRAM stand for?
notes.back: Nonvolatile Random Access Memory.
notes.explanation: The standards name it alongside RAM and ROM.
notes.source: Aviation Mechanic General, Airframe, and Powerplant ACS Companion Guide, “Appendix: Abbreviations and Acronyms”, PDF p. 27
notes.evidence: NVRAM Nonvolatile Random Access Memory

notes.front: What turns a basic alternating current generator into a basic DC generator?
notes.back: Replacing its slip rings with a commutator.
notes.explanation: The commutator makes current flow always the same way through the external circuit.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Generator Principles”, PDF p. 566
notes.evidence: By replacing the slip rings of the basic AC generator with two half cylinders, called a commutator, a basic DC generator is obtained.

notes.front: During an inspection, a DC generator’s commutator looks dull and slightly dirty. What must the technician not do?
notes.back: B) Apply a light film of oil to it
notes.choices:
A) Clean it carefully to avoid scratching it
B) Apply a light film of oil to it
C) Check the brushes for wear
D) Follow the manufacturer’s instructions
notes.choicesExplained: A) Careful cleaning is what the Handbook asks for. C) Brush condition is a normal inspection item. D) Following the manufacturer’s instructions is always right.
notes.explanation: Oil or grease must never be used on a commutator.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Armature”, PDF p. 571
notes.evidence: Oil or grease must never be used on a commutator

notes.front: Why is a series wound generator never used as an aeroplane generator?
notes.back: Its voltage regulation is very poor.
notes.explanation: Aircraft generators have their fields connected either in shunt or in compound.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Series Wound DC Generators”, PDF p. 574
notes.evidence: Since the series wound generator has such poor regulation, it is never employed as an airplane generator.

notes.front: In a shunt wound generator, how is the field winding connected, and what happens to terminal voltage as load increases?
notes.back: In parallel with the external circuit; terminal voltage falls as load increases.
notes.explanation: More load means more armature current and a larger voltage drop in the armature.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Shunt Wound DC Generators”, PDF p. 574
notes.evidence: Any increase in load causes a decrease in the terminal or output voltage, and any decrease in load causes an increase in terminal voltage

notes.front: Where are compound wound generators used?
notes.back: Where voltage regulation is of prime importance.
notes.explanation: They combine a series and a shunt winding to use the advantages of each.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Compound Wound DC Generators”, PDF p. 575
notes.evidence: Compound generators are used where voltage regulation is of prime importance.

notes.front: A generator’s series field aids its shunt field. What is it called?
notes.back: Cumulative compounded.
notes.explanation: If the series field opposes the shunt field instead, it is differentially compounded.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Compound Wound DC Generators”, PDF p. 575
notes.evidence: If the series field aids the shunt field, the generator is said to be cumulative compounded.

notes.front: Why must emery cloth never be used to seat generator brushes?
notes.back: It contains conductive material that causes arcing between brushes and commutator bars.
notes.explanation: Brushes are seated with 000 or finer sandpaper instead, pulled in the direction of rotation.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Condition of Generator Brushes”, PDF p. 577
notes.evidence: Under no circumstances should emery cloth or similar abrasives be used for seating brushes (or smoothing commutators), since they contain conductive materials that cause arcing between brushes and commutator bars.

notes.front: In the right-hand motor rule, what do the index finger, second finger and thumb show?
notes.back: Index finger: magnetic field; second finger: current flow; thumb: direction the wire moves.
notes.explanation: It finds the direction a current-carrying wire moves in a magnetic field.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Developing Torque”, PDF p. 579
notes.evidence: if the index finger of the right hand is pointed in the direction of the magnetic field and the second finger in the direction of current flow, the thumb indicates the direction the current carrying wire moves.

notes.front: A technician needs to predict which way a current-carrying conductor in a motor will be pushed by the field. Which rule applies?
notes.back: D) The right-hand motor rule
notes.choices:
A) The left-hand rule for a conductor
B) Kirchhoff’s voltage law
C) Lenz’s law
D) The right-hand motor rule
notes.choicesExplained: A) That left-hand rule gives the direction of the field around a conductor, not its motion. B) Kirchhoff’s voltage law concerns voltages around a loop. C) Lenz’s law gives the direction of an induced current.
notes.explanation: The right-hand motor rule gives the direction a current-carrying wire moves in a magnetic field.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Developing Torque”, PDF p. 579
notes.evidence: The right-hand motor rule can be used to determine the direction a current carrying wire moves in a magnetic field.

notes.front: What is the principal advantage of a series DC motor, and how does its speed behave?
notes.back: High starting torque; it runs fast with a light load and slow with a heavy load.
notes.explanation: Its low-resistance windings let it draw a large starting current through both field and armature.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Series DC Motor”, PDF p. 583
notes.evidence: This starting current, in passing through both the field and armature windings, produces a high starting torque, which is the series motor’s principal advantage.

notes.front: When is a shunt DC motor particularly suitable?
notes.back: When constant speed is wanted and high starting torque is not needed.
notes.explanation: Its speed varies very little with load, but its starting torque is lower than a series motor’s.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Shunt DC Motor”, PDF p. 583
notes.evidence: This motor is particularly suitable for use when constant speed is desired and when high starting torque is not needed.

notes.front: A starter must turn over a heavy engine from rest. Which type of DC motor suits it best?
notes.back: B) Series motor
notes.choices:
A) Shunt motor
B) Series motor
C) Synchronous motor
D) Shaded pole motor
notes.choicesExplained: A) A shunt motor’s starting torque is lower than a series motor’s. C) A synchronous motor is an alternating current motor with little starting torque. D) A shaded pole motor has low starting torque and suits small fans.
notes.explanation: A series motor gives high starting torque, which is what a heavy starting load needs.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Series DC Motor”, PDF p. 583
notes.evidence: If high starting torque is needed under heavy load conditions, series motors have many applications.

notes.front: How does an intermittent-duty motor differ from a continuous-duty motor?
notes.back: It may run only for short periods and must then cool; a continuous-duty motor can run at rated power for long periods.
notes.explanation: Run for long periods at full load, an intermittent-duty motor overheats.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Types of Duty”, PDF p. 585
notes.evidence: Motors built for intermittent duty can be operated for short periods only and, then, must be allowed to cool before being operated again.

notes.front: Why does swapping the two supply wires of a DC motor not reverse it?
notes.back: It reverses the magnetism of both field and armature, so the torque stays the same way.
notes.explanation: Reversing the current in either the armature or the field alone reverses rotation.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Reversing Motor Direction”, PDF p. 585
notes.evidence: If the wires connecting the motor to an external source are interchanged, the direction of rotation is not reversed, since changing these wires reverses the magnetism of both field and armature and leaves the torque in the same direction as before.

notes.front: What sets the speed of rotation of an alternating current motor?
notes.back: The number of poles and the frequency of the supply: rpm = 120 × frequency ÷ poles.
notes.explanation: On 400-cycle aircraft systems this gives high speeds, suited to small, high-speed rotors through reduction gears.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “AC Motors”, PDF p. 588
notes.evidence: The speed of rotation of an AC motor depends upon the number of poles and the frequency of the electrical source of power

notes.front: What are the two general types of alternating current motor used in aircraft?
notes.back: Induction motors and synchronous motors.
notes.explanation: Three-phase induction motors handle large loads; synchronous motors run at constant speed.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Types of AC Motors”, PDF p. 588
notes.evidence: There are two general types of AC motors used in aircraft systems: induction motors and synchronous motors.

notes.front: A propeller synchroniser system needs a motor running at a constant speed locked to supply frequency. Which type?
notes.back: C) Three-phase synchronous motor
notes.choices:
A) Series DC motor
B) Shaded pole induction motor
C) Three-phase synchronous motor
D) Single-phase induction motor
notes.choicesExplained: B) Shaded pole motors have weak starting torque and suit small fans. A) A series motor’s speed changes with load. D) Single-phase induction motors run low-power devices like shut-off valves, with slip.
notes.explanation: Three-phase synchronous motors run at constant synchronous speed and are used for propeller synchroniser systems.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Types of AC Motors”, PDF p. 588
notes.evidence: Three-phase synchronous motors operate at constant synchronous speeds and are commonly used to operate flux gate compasses and propeller synchronizer systems.

notes.front: An induction motor’s field turns at 8,000 rpm and its rotor at 7,600 rpm. What is the slip?
notes.back: D) 5 percent
notes.choices:
A) 400 percent
B) 0.5 percent
C) 95 percent
D) 5 percent
notes.choicesExplained: A) That is the speed difference in rpm, not a percentage. C) That is the rotor speed as a share of synchronous speed. B) The decimal point is misplaced.
notes.explanation: Slip is the speed difference as a percentage of synchronous speed: 400 ÷ 8,000 is 5 percent.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Induction Motor Slip”, PDF p. 590
notes.evidence: This difference in speed is called slip and is expressed as a percentage of the synchronous speed.

notes.front: Why is a brushless alternator more efficient?
notes.back: It has no brushes to wear down or arc at high altitude.
notes.explanation: An integral exciter with a rectified rotating armature feeds the main field, removing the need for brushes.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Brushless Alternator”, PDF p. 598
notes.evidence: Brushless Alternator This design is more efficient because there are no brushes to wear down or to arc at high altitudes.

notes.front: An alternator’s rotor speed is raised while its number of poles stays the same. What happens to its output frequency?
notes.back: C) It rises
notes.choices:
A) It is unchanged
B) It falls
C) It rises
D) It becomes direct current
notes.choicesExplained: B) A lower frequency comes from a lower speed. A) Frequency depends on rotor speed as well as poles. D) Only rectification turns alternating into direct current.
notes.explanation: Alternator frequency depends on rotor speed and the number of poles: the faster the speed, the higher the frequency.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Alternator Frequency”, PDF p. 599
notes.evidence: The frequency of the alternator voltage depends upon the speed of rotation of the rotor and the number of poles. The faster the speed, the higher the frequency

notes.front: In a balanced wye-connected alternator, how does line voltage compare with phase voltage?
notes.back: Line voltage is 1.73 times the phase voltage; line current equals phase current.
notes.explanation: In a delta connection it is the other way round: line current is 1.73 times phase current.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Wye Connection (Three-Phase)”, PDF p. 597
notes.evidence: For balanced conditions, the line voltage is 1.73 times the phase voltage.

notes.front: If resistance in a generator’s field circuit is increased, what happens to its output voltage?
notes.back: It falls: less field current flows, and the magnetic field weakens.
notes.explanation: The field current is the one factor of output voltage that can be conveniently controlled.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Regulation of Generator Voltage”, PDF p. 600
notes.evidence: If the rheostat is set to increase the resistance in the field circuit, less current flows through the field winding and the strength of the magnetic field in which the armature rotates decreases.

notes.front: What is the purpose of a reverse current cut-out relay?
notes.back: To disconnect the battery from the generator automatically when generator voltage falls below battery voltage.
notes.explanation: Without it, the battery would discharge through the generator armature and drive the generator as a motor; light aircraft often carry it in a three-unit regulator.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Regulation of Generator Voltage”, PDF p. 602
notes.evidence: The purpose of the reverse current cut-out relay is to automatically disconnect the battery from the generator when the generator voltage is less than the battery voltage.

notes.front: A generator’s output voltage is too high. What does its voltage regulator adjust to bring it down?
notes.back: A) The field current, reducing it
notes.choices:
A) The field current, reducing it
B) The number of armature turns
C) The engine speed
D) The battery voltage
notes.choicesExplained: C) Engine speed is not something the regulator conveniently controls. B) Armature turns are fixed in construction. D) The battery does not set generator output.
notes.explanation: Field current is the one output factor that can be conveniently controlled; less field current means lower voltage.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Regulation of Generator Voltage”, PDF p. 600
notes.evidence: Among the factors, which determine the voltage output of a generator, only one, the strength of the field current, can be conveniently controlled.

notes.front: Which safety equipment does the Handbook name for working on electrical equipment?
notes.back: Rubber gloves, safety glasses and rubber or grounded safety mats, among others.
notes.explanation: Proper safety equipment physically protects the technician and gives psychological assurance.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Electrical Safety”, PDF p. 22
notes.evidence: The use of rubber gloves, safety glasses, rubber or grounded safety mats, and other safety equipment contributes to the overall safety of the technician working on or with electrical equipment.

notes.front: A technician is about to troubleshoot a live bus on the bench. Which preparation matches the Handbook’s electrical safety advice?
notes.back: B) Wear rubber gloves and safety glasses and stand on a rubber mat
notes.choices:
A) Remove rubber gloves for better feel
B) Wear rubber gloves and safety glasses and stand on a rubber mat
C) Stand on bare concrete to stay grounded
D) Rely on care alone, since equipment only gives false confidence
notes.choicesExplained: A) Rubber gloves are part of the protective equipment named. C) The Handbook names rubber or grounded safety mats, not bare floors. D) The Handbook says equipment gives both psychological assurance and physical protection.
notes.explanation: Rubber gloves, safety glasses and rubber or grounded mats all add to safety around electrical equipment.
notes.source: Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook–General (FAA-H-8083-30B, 2023), Chapter 12, “Electrical Safety”, PDF p. 22
notes.evidence: Wearing or use of proper safety equipment can provide a psychological assurance and physically protect the user at the same time.

notes.front: Of RAM, ROM and NVRAM, which one’s full name marks it as nonvolatile?
notes.back: NVRAM: Nonvolatile Random Access Memory.
notes.explanation: Its expansion adds “nonvolatile” to random access memory.
notes.source: Aviation Mechanic General, Airframe, and Powerplant ACS Companion Guide, “Appendix: Abbreviations and Acronyms”, PDF p. 27
notes.evidence: NVRAM Nonvolatile Random Access Memory
